clue.text: Work out chairman's bust on board

definitions.note: a carved bust fixed to the bow of a ship, 'on board' a vessel

parts.note: to work out a sum is to figure it
the head of a company or committee chairs it

explanation.surface: Someone calculates that the company chairman has gone bankrupt while serving on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like bankruptcy and 'board' a company board; both turn nautical.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved bust or figure mounted on a sailing ship's prow is its traditional emblem.

clue.text: Stable business

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: an adjective for solid and steady, and a noun for a trading company.

clue.text: Elderly mounting clicking

definitions.meaning: climbing aboard a horse or bus
two people hitting it off, forming a rapport

explanation.surface: An old person climbs up while something clicks.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: three separate senses of the same phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means ageing, boarding a vehicle, and having a good relationship with someone.

clue.text: Top person bet gold goes up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to lay money is to bet it
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A top person's wager on gold rises in value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' turns LAYOR around, since this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the monarch's family sits at the very top of society.

clue.text: Shelter to put up pauper

parts.note: a haven is a safe place of refuge

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting a word up means writing it from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A refuge exists to house a poor person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' looks like offering lodging, but it reverses 'to' to OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor person, one lacking wealth, is contrasted with the 'haves'.

clue.text: Entire river's charms

parts.note: entire means all
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England, plus the 's

explanation.surface: A whole river's attractions are praised.
explanation.definitionFit: Allures are attractive qualities, the enticements that draw someone in.

clue.text: Go crazy when rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: bats is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Someone loses their mind after being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is the noun, an attempt, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a go and having a stab both mean making an attempt at something.

clue.text: It is not commonly a corrupting influence

definitions.meaning: dialect or colloquial contraction of it isn't, written with an apostrophe
a trace of contamination or moral pollution

explanation.surface: Someone insists that something is not usually a bad influence.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the slangy contraction 't'ain't'; 'commonly' flags informal speech.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a trace of something bad that spoils or contaminates.

clue.text: Magistrates and journalists bear great weight

parts.note: magistrates collectively are the bench
the press is journalists as a body

explanation.surface: Courts and reporters carry heavy responsibilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear great weight' sounds like carrying influence; it is a gym exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A weightlifting exercise in which you lie on a bench and push a heavy barbell upward.

clue.text: Sea creature unadorned with pinch of salt

indicators.note: the word for unadorned pinches, or squeezes in, the salt

parts.note: plain, bare
NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt

explanation.surface: A sea creature served plain, with just a pinch of salt.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt is given by its chemical formula, sodium chloride.
explanation.definitionFit: A small marine crustacean that clings to rocks and ship hulls.

clue.text: Mole's friend is irritable

definitions.meaning: the water rat who befriends Mole in The Wind in the Willows

explanation.surface: A friend of a mole is grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is the riverbank character in Kenneth Grahame's children's book, and the word also means short-tempered.

clue.text: Very East European to be losing head, that's common

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word drops off

parts.note: a person from Bulgaria

explanation.surface: An Eastern European about to be beheaded is described as quite ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse, unrefined person is one who is common, lacking taste or manners.

clue.text: Racer over 8 furlongs holds nothing back, being one that works hard before Ascot

definitions.text: one that works hard before Ascot

indicators.note: the racer contains the next piece inside it

parts.note: eight furlongs make a mile, so a horse or runner suited to that distance is a miler

indicators.note: back means the word for nothing is reversed

parts.note: nil is nothing

explanation.surface: A racehorse holding nothing in reserve before the Ascot race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot, the royal race meeting in England, is famous for extravagant hats, so a hatmaker is busy beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatmaker is flat out before Royal Ascot, where elaborate headwear is the tradition.

clue.text: Nick excluding Switzerland

parts.note: not, as in 'not including'
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A man called Nick is not from Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name but is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cut or indentation in an edge is a nick.

clue.text: Lack of progress disturbed antagonist

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An opponent is unsettled by getting nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is the state of being still and making no headway.

clue.text: Water tower

parts.note: a tank on stilts, but read as a vessel that tows on water

explanation.walkthrough: A tower is something that tows, here on water.
explanation.definitionFit: A small powerful boat that pulls ships around a harbour.

clue.text: Drool dodderingly about clergyman turning up in wartime operation

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the next piece
doddering means tottering unsteadily, so the letters wobble into a new order
in a down entry, turning up means read upward, backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for reverend

explanation.surface: An old man slobbers around a vicar who appears in a war story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodderingly' rearranges DROOL to O-LORD, which goes 'about' VER, the 'turning up' of REV.
explanation.definitionFit: Operation Overlord was the codename for the Allied invasion of Normandy in 1944.

clue.text: The Parisian visiting most of close outside the church

indicators.note: the French word goes in, visiting the shortened word
most of a word loses its final letter

parts.note: secure, fastened shut
la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: A French woman calls at a cathedral close outside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like a cathedral precinct; it is the adjective 'secure'.
explanation.definitionFit: Secular means worldly, not connected with religious or church matters.

clue.text: Use ol' Mini that's clapped out? Get much bigger car

indicators.note: clapped out means worn out and broken, so the letters fall apart and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Advice to someone whose old Mini has died: buy a far larger vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mini is a small British car, so the upgrade is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious car, far bigger than a Mini.

clue.text: Man marooned on Treasure Island long time finds large-leaved plant

parts.note: Ben Gunn is the castaway in Stevenson's novel
an era is a long period

explanation.surface: A castaway, after years alone, discovers a giant-leafed plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunnera is a genus of plants with enormous rhubarb-like foliage, often grown beside ponds.

clue.text: Succeed with a herb placed around top of escalope

indicators.note: the herb is set around the following letter

parts.note: chive is a herb

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: garnish an escalope with herbs and it will turn out well.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve is to accomplish or succeed in doing something.

clue.text: The Royal Marines heading lowly sailor's vessel

indicators.note: the marines head, come before, the sailor

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman, the lowest rank

explanation.surface: Marines lead a humble sailor's ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship but is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum flask is a vessel that keeps drinks hot or cold.

clue.text: English parliamentarian in international storm

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An English MP is caught in a global storm.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a full international game of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent windy storm.

clue.text: A person from the Far North returning in shock

indicators.note: returning means going back, read in reverse

parts.note: a Lapp is from Lapland in Arctic Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A traveller back from the Arctic is in shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to shock or horrify someone.

clue.text: Flag and fade away

explanation.surface: A flag fades in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: To peter out is to diminish gradually, and flagging energy similarly dwindles.

clue.text: Simple detective joke, as some would tell it

indicators.note: telling means speaking, so this is how the phrase is pronounced

parts.note: Holmes is the fictional detective; a pun is a joke

explanation.surface: An unsophisticated sleuth's gag, as some people relate it.
explanation.walkthrough: The L in Holmes is silent, so it is said 'Homes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun means plain and unsophisticated, like home-woven cloth.

clue.text: Weapon pierces a breastplate to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A weapon partly penetrates armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabre is a heavy cavalry sword with a curved blade.

clue.text: Turn corner

definitions.meaning: a short performance or act in a show
a difficult situation, a tight place

explanation.surface: An instruction to a driver to go round a bend.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a slot in a show, and being in a spot is being cornered.

clue.text: Teen cried out — act as peacemaker

indicators.note: out signals the letters are rearranged, despite reading with cried as a phrase

explanation.surface: A teenager yells, and someone steps in to calm things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cried out' reads as a phrase, but 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercede is to intervene on someone's behalf to settle a dispute.

clue.text: Reactionary fellow that's full of gas

definitions.meaning: after Colonel ..., a pompous cartoon character embodying diehard conservatism

explanation.surface: A conservative man is full of hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp was a British newspaper cartoon figure of a blustering old reactionary.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a pompous old conservative and a gas-filled airship.

clue.text: Standard choice of letters from the middle of the alphabet

definitions.text: choice of letters from the middle of the alphabet
definitions.meaning: four letters drawn from the central stretch M to R

explanation.surface: A typical selection of letters taken from the alphabet's centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a standard or usual pattern; its letters N, O, R, M all sit mid-alphabet.

clue.text: Hamlet's resolution

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Hamlet resolves to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' looks like the play; it is a small village.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is a community of houses, and also an agreement ending a dispute.
